items.title: What is a datacenter proxy?
items.description: A datacenter proxy is a proxy service based on datacenter servers, using IP addresses allocated by datacenters. Compared to residential proxies, datacenter proxies have higher speed, larger bandwidth and lower cost, suitable for application scenarios with high performance requirements.

items.title: What's the difference between datacenter and residential proxies?
items.description: Datacenter proxies are based on server IPs with fast speed, large bandwidth and low cost, but may be more easily identified; residential proxies are based on real user IPs with higher anonymity but relatively slower speed and higher cost. The choice depends on your specific needs.

items.title: How fast are datacenter proxies?
items.description: IPFlex datacenter proxies have an average latency of less than 100 milliseconds, with single IP bandwidth up to 10Gbps. Based on global top-tier datacenter infrastructure, ensuring ultra-fast network access experience, especially suitable for applications with extremely high speed requirements.

items.title: What protocols and ports are supported?
items.description: IPFlex datacenter proxies support HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS5 protocols, providing multiple port options. Support both username/password authentication and IP whitelist authentication to meet different application access needs.

items.title: How stable are datacenter proxies?
items.description: IPFlex datacenter proxies provide 99.9% uptime guarantee with professional operations team 24/7 monitoring. Based on enterprise-grade datacenter infrastructure, ensuring high availability and stability of services.

items.title: How to choose the right datacenter node?
items.description: It's recommended to choose datacenter nodes closer to target servers for optimal performance. IPFlex deploys nodes in 100+ datacenters globally, you can choose the optimal geographic location based on your business needs.
